newsitem.title: USA: Maine governor signs phone fee cut legislation.
newsitem.headline: Maine governor signs phone fee cut legislation.

text.p: Maine Gov. Angus King Thursday signed legislation ordering Maine Public Utilities Commission to cut the price of in-state long distance phone charges.

Regulators are authorized to have local phone companies reduce the access fees they charge long distance providers on in-state toll calls to the same level they charge those providers for interstate toll calls by May 30, 1999.
"This bill is more important to more Maine people than just about any bill we've enacted this session," King said at a State House signing ceremony.
King and other supporters of the measure contend reducing the access fees will lead to lower phone rates by encouraging competition for the in-state market between long distance providers.
Maine's in-state access rates are amoung the highest in the country and the measure signed Thursday could reduce in-state telephone rates by up to 70 percent in the next two years, King said.
